frontier.hypothesis: Every sanctioned axis on func_80078654 is now measured dead across five distinct modalities, and the forced-decomposition theorem explains why: the correct disposition is an owner escalation, not further grinding.
frontier.mechanism: The target's three-callee-save census plus its 0xC/0x14 displacements force all twelve buffer accesses onto one pseudo (reg_n_refs 13, pri 3979), while the walk pointer's reference count is pinned at 5 with a ceiling of 8 (pri 2448) and free references are impossible (s6 pinning, s7 no transfer / no sharing) - so allocno_compare can never order the walk pointer first, and its tie-break is strict in the parameter's favour.
frontier.next_probe: The driver decides exhaustion, not the session; if it assigns `escalation` modality, both endgame gates are already measured and BOTH FAIL, so the entry is the standing 2026-07-27 auto-ruling shape (REFUSED / OWNER-ACCEPTED INCOMPLETE), citing scan_hand_coded tier=LOW score=0/8 for gate 1 and the absence of any citable SOTN-master RA-coercion precedent for gate 2.

frontier.hypothesis: If a further grinding session is assigned before escalation, the only premise of the theorem that is inductive rather than deductive is premise (3): that EVERY pseudo carrying a proper subset of the twelve accesses must be live across a call.
frontier.mechanism: Premise (3) rests on four measured splits, not on an exhaustive enumeration. A split confined to a call-free window would not need a callee-save - the target's only such window is the `lw $v0,0x14($s1); addiu $v0,$v0,0xC; sw $v0,0x14($s1)` RMW pair at the end of each block.
frontier.next_probe: Build the RMW-window-only split (a pointer holding arg0's value created and killed strictly between the AddPrim call and the block end, so it never crosses a call) and check with s5/eval.sh whether it (a) survives cse, (b) keeps three callee-saves, and (c) moves reg_n_refs(72) below 13. Note the displacement argument predicts it must still be a pure ALIAS, not `arg0 + 5`, to keep `20($sN)`; a two-reference alias is also the shape cse is most likely to delete.
